messages.content: What's the population in New York right now?

function.name: time_converter
function.description: Converts the local time of user's region to the target region's local time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_timezone.description: The timezone of the user in string format. Example: 'Pacific Time (US & Canada)'

target_timezone.description: The target timezone in string format where user wants to know the local time. Example: 'Eastern Time (US & Canada)'

time.description: The local time of user's timezone in string format (24 hr format). Optional parameter. Example: '15:30:00'

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time population figures. The most recent estimates put New York City’s population at around 8.5 million people as of the last census and subsequent projections, but I can’t provide an exact number “right now.”
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What's the population in New York right now?" They want current population. We need to use the time_converter function? No, that's for converting times. There's no function for population. So we should respond that we don't have real-time data. We can provide approximate or mention that we can't fetch live data. According to policy, we cannot fabricate. So we should say we don't have up-to-date info.
